questions.q: Which of the following collections are sets? Justify your answer in one sentence each. (i) The collection of all months of a year beginning with the letter J. (ii) The collection of ten most talented writers of India. (iii) The collection of all natural numbers less than 100.
questions.a: (i) Yes — it is well-defined: we can objectively check if a month starts with J (January, June, July). (ii) No — "most talented" is subjective; different people may have different opinions, so membership is not well-defined. (iii) Yes — for any given number, we can definitively check if it is a natural number < 100. A wrong answer reveals the student confuses "well-defined" with "finite" or "small", or thinks subjective descriptions can be sets.

questions.q: A student writes: "The set of all integers x such that x² = 4 is {2}." Explain why this answer is incomplete and write the correct set in both roster and set-builder forms.
questions.a: The equation x² = 4 has two integer solutions: x = 2 and x = -2. The student missed -2, likely because they only considered positive square roots. Correct roster form: {2, -2} or {-2, 2} (order irrelevant). Correct set-builder form: {x : x ∈ Z and x² = 4}. A wrong answer reveals the student does not apply the "well-defined" criterion to negative integers or forgets that square roots yield both positive and negative values in Z.

questions.q: Write the set A = {x : x is a positive integer and x² < 40} in roster form. Then write the set B = {1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36} in set-builder form using the variable n ∈ N.
questions.a: For A: positive integers with square < 40 are 1²=1, 2²=4, 3²=9, 4²=16, 5²=25, 6²=36; 7²=49 > 40. So A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. For B: elements are perfect squares of natural numbers 1 through 6. Set-builder: B = {n² : n ∈ N and 1 ≤ n ≤ 6} or B = {x : x = n², n ∈ N, n ≤ 6}. A wrong answer reveals confusion between the element variable (x) and the parameter (n), or inability to recognise the pattern "square of natural number".

questions.q: Consider the sets: X = {x : x ∈ N and 2x - 1 = 0} and Y = {x : x ∈ Z and 2x - 1 = 0}. Are X and Y equal? Explain your reasoning by solving for x in each domain.
questions.a: Solving 2x - 1 = 0 gives x = 1/2. In X, domain is N (natural numbers); 1/2 ∉ N, so X = φ (empty set). In Y, domain is Z (integers); 1/2 ∉ Z, so Y = φ. Since both are empty sets, X = Y = φ. A wrong answer (e.g., saying they are not equal because domains differ) reveals the student does not understand that equality of sets depends only on elements, not on the defining condition's domain, or that φ is unique.

questions.q: A student claims: "The set {a, e, i, o, u} and the set {x : x is a vowel in the English alphabet} are not equal because the first uses letters and the second uses a variable x." Evaluate this claim and correct the misconception.
questions.a: The claim is false. The two sets are equal because they contain exactly the same elements: a, e, i, o, u. The variable x in set-builder notation is a dummy variable — it does not become an element of the set. The description {x : x is a vowel...} means "the set of all objects x such that x is a vowel"; the elements are the vowels themselves, not the letter x. A wrong evaluation reveals the student confuses the placeholder variable with the actual elements, a fundamental misunderstanding of set-builder notation.

questions.q: Construct a set in set-builder form that satisfies all three conditions: (a) It is a subset of Z (integers), (b) It has exactly 5 elements, (c) Its elements are symmetric about 0 (i.e., if k is in the set, -k is also in the set). Write the set in both set-builder and roster forms.
questions.a: One valid answer: Roster form: {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}. Set-builder form: {x : x ∈ Z and -2 ≤ x ≤ 2} or {x : x ∈ Z and x² ≤ 4}. The symmetry condition requires 0 to be included (since -0 = 0) and pairs (±k). With exactly 5 elements, the only symmetric integer set is {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}. A poor answer (e.g., {-3, -1, 0, 1, 3} or missing 0) reveals the student does not grasp "symmetric about 0" or the uniqueness of the empty set's role in symmetry.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects, where "well-defined" means for any given object, we can ______ decide whether it belongs to the collection or not.

Fill in the blank: Now we formalise: a ______ set requires that for any candidate (e.g., a student's name), there is an objective yes/no answer to "Does this belong?" — no subjective judgement like "talented" or "best".
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can: (1) Determine whether a given collection qualifies as a set by applying the well-defined criterion, (2) Correctly use ∈ and ∉ notation to describe membership, (3) Represent the same set in both roster form (listing elements) and set-builder form (describing common property), (4) Identify and use standard set notations N.
